findings.title: Stop issuing a no-op `updateMany` on every cache refresh
Throw TRPCError instead of generic Error in deleteCache handler
"Delete cached data" is offered for credentials the handler will always reject
Format the cache timestamp with the user's locale, not hard-coded "en-US"
Respect the calendar-cache feature flag when fetching cache status
Avoid `npx tsx` fetching an undeclared dependency at runtime
Remove the stale warning comment in the migration

response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Stop issuing a no-op `updateMany` on every cache refresh

Affected:
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022-1024
- packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts:400-405

Explanation:
`updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object and relies on Prisma's `@updatedAt` to bump the timestamp. Prisma only sets `@updatedAt` when it actually runs an update, and with an empty `data` it may run no update at all. If so, `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` never changes and the stated goal is not met.

The call still adds an extra DB round-trip to every webhook-triggered cache refresh. That runs in the hot path of `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`, so a failure here (for example, a DB hiccup) makes the whole refresh reject after the cache was already written.

The UI added in this PR reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt` (via `cacheUpdatedAt`), not `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, so this write appears to have no consumer. The same goes for the new `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` selects in `user.ts`.

Fix: remove the call. If the timestamp really is needed, set it explicitly and do it best-effort.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
// Either remove entirely, or set explicitly and don't fail the refresh:
await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {
  updatedAt: new Date(),
}).catch((e) => log.warn("Failed to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt", e));
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Throw TRPCError instead of generic Error in deleteCache handler

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:24-26

Explanation:
A plain `Error` is surfaced by tRPC as `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500). That hides a normal authorization or not-found outcome as a server fault, pollutes error monitoring, and may leak the message differently across environments.

Use `TRPCError` with `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN`.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
import { TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";
...
if (!credential) {
  throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: "Credential not found" });
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: "Delete cached data" is offered for credentials the handler will always reject

Affected:
- packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:69-111
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:17-22

Explanation:
The cache actions show whenever `hasCache` is true, including for delegation credentials and team-owned credentials. The handler, however, only accepts credentials where `userId === user.id`. Delegation credentials are not stored as user-owned `Credential` rows, so for them the delete action always fails with an error toast. This depends on how delegation credentials are represented outside this diff, hence the lowered severity.

Fix: hide the delete-cache item when `delegationCredentialId` is set, or extend the handler's ownership check to cover those credentials.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
const canDeleteCache = hasCache && !delegationCredentialId;
...
{canDeleteCache && ( /* delete cached data item */ )}
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Implementation
Title: Format the cache timestamp with the user's locale, not hard-coded "en-US"

Affected:
- packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:88-94

Explanation:
The timestamp is always formatted with `"en-US"` while the label around it is translated. Non-US users therefore see US date ordering (M/D/YY), which is ambiguous.

Use the active i18n language from `useLocale()`.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
const { t, i18n } = useLocale();
...
new Intl.DateTimeFormat(i18n.language, { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })
  .format(new Date(cacheUpdatedAt))
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Implementation
Title: Respect the calendar-cache feature flag when fetching cache status

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-29

Explanation:
The handler always instantiates the concrete `CalendarCacheRepository`. A `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` exists for when calendar-cache is disabled, and this method was added to it, but the handler bypasses it. As a result, every `connectedCalendars` call runs a `groupBy` query even when the feature is off, and cache UI can show stale rows.

Fix: obtain the repository through the same flag-aware factory used elsewhere (for example, `CalendarCache.init`/`getCalendarCacheRepository` or equivalent), or check the flag first.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const cacheRepository = await getCalendarCacheRepositoryRespectingFlag(); // existing flag-aware factory
const cacheStatuses = credentialIds.length
  ? await cacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds)
  : [];
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Make test-gcal-webhooks.sh portable and path-independent

Affected:
- scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5
- scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:11-18
- scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:28-31
- scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68

Explanation:
- `sed -i ''` only works with BSD/macOS sed. On GNU sed (Linux/CI), `''` is treated as the script and the substitution fails.
- `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves against the caller's current directory, not the script's location. Running the script from the repo root writes to the wrong file, and may create a stray `.env` outside the repo.
- `cleanup` always exits 0, even on failure paths (rate limit, no URL), so callers cannot detect failure.
- When reusing an already-running tmole, the URL comes from `/tmp/tmole.log`, which may be missing or stale.

Proposed fix:
~~~bash
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ENV_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../.env"
cleanup() { local code=${1:-0}; ...; exit "$code"; }
# portable in-place edit
tmp=$(mktemp) && sed -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE" > "$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
~~~

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Avoid `npx tsx` fetching an undeclared dependency at runtime

Affected:
- apps/web/package.json:11

Explanation:
If `tsx` is not declared in devDependencies, `npx tsx` downloads whatever version is latest on each fresh environment. That makes the dev tooling non-reproducible and requires network access. Inside a yarn script, `npx` is also unnecessary.

Fix: add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly.

Proposed fix:
~~~json
"dev:cron": "tsx cron-tester.ts"
~~~

## 8) Severity: INFO | Type: Doc
Title: Remove the stale warning comment in the migration

Affected:
- packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:1-6

Explanation:
The auto-generated header says the column is added "without a default value" and that this "is not possible if the table is not empty". The SQL actually uses `DEFAULT NOW()`. The comment is misleading to anyone auditing migrations, so remove it.

Proposed fix:
~~~sql
-- AlterTable: add updatedAt with default to backfill existing rows
ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW();
~~~
